dataset_name: MGS MOLA MEGDR topography, 128 pixels/degree (463 m), PDS4
citation: Smith, D. E., Zuber, M. T., Neumann, G. A., Guinness, E. A., & Slavney, S. (2003). Mars Global Surveyor Laser Altimeter Mission Experiment Gridded Data Record, MGS-M-MOLA-5-MEGDR-L3-V1.0. NASA Planetary Data System (PDS4 bundle urn:nasa:pds:mgs_mola_topography_derived). Instrument: Smith, D. E., et al. (2001). Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter: Experiment summary after the first year of global mapping of Mars. Journal of Geophysical Research, 106(E10), 23689-23722. https://doi.org/10.1029/2000JE001364
license: NASA data, public domain; cite the PDS dataset and Smith et al. (2001).
vertical_datum: Topography in metres: planetary radius minus the MOLA areoid radius (a gravity equipotential surface, degree and order 50); planetocentric, east-positive, IAU 2000; simple cylindrical (equirectangular) projection on a 3,396 km sphere.

checks.detail: The projection is not true-scale here: a pixel covers 439 x 463 m on the ground. Layer 3 resamples onto a local metric grid.
No nodata value; voids cannot be told from data.

limitations: Each pixel is the median of the laser shots in a 1/128 degree bin; where a bin holds no shot the producer interpolated a value (PDS: about 55 % of bins near the equator hold at least one shot, with gaps up to 12 km between ground tracks), so slopes there are smoothed. There is no void value: interpolated pixels cannot be told from measured ones.
463 m pixels cannot resolve rover-scale slopes, rocks, or wheel traction; metrics describe regional terrain only.

Vertical: about 40 cm resolution; the PDS catalog estimates about 30 m absolute long-wavelength radial orbit error and about 400 m ground-spot location uncertainty at 400 km range. USGS puts the total elevation uncertainty at no better than 3 m (areoid error included).
The equirectangular pixel is only 463 m east-west on the equator (463 m x cos(latitude) on the ground); Layer 3 resamples it onto a local metric grid.
Not the USGS Astropedia 463 m mosaic: that product is a half-pixel-shifted, 2 x 2-averaged resampling of this data and is smoother.
processing: Pixels copied on the source grid; no resampling.

details.instrument: Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA), Mars Global Surveyor
details.product_type: MEGDR median topography ('megt'), 128 pixels/degree, one PDS4 product per 44 x 90 degree tile
details.acquired: MOLA mapping and extended mission to 2001-06-30 (product label: 1997-09-15 to 2001-06-30); product created 2003
details.processing: Crossover-adjusted PEDR shots binned to 1/128 degree; areoid from the Goddard Mars potential model GMM3 (mgm1025), degree and order 50 (per the product label).
details.storage: big-endian int16 metres, no nodata, read through the PDS4 label (GDAL PDS4 driver)
